briefing.headline: OpenAI's Q* successor drives AI race as China ramps up compute investments.

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: The global AI race intensifies with major advancements in frontier models from US and Chinese firms, amid growing concerns over safety and regulatory gaps. Investment in AI infrastructure hit record highs this quarter, while emerging threats like deepfakes underscore the need for robust security protocols. DialectForge's protocol continues to gain traction for securing multi-agent systems in real-world applications.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI unveiled its Q*2 model with enhanced reasoning capabilities, while Anthropic released Claude 4, focusing on ethical AI alignment. Google and DeepSeek pushed multimodal advancements, with Meta open-sourcing Llama 4 for broader access; xAI's Grok 3 integrated real-time data for enterprise use, heightening competition from Chinese players like Baidu's Ernie Bot 5.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: AI safety efforts advanced with new frameworks from the EU AI Act updates, addressing emerging vulnerabilities in large-scale deployments. Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems, but DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level, offering secure communication for AI agents in BCI and IoT environments.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: Nvidia dominated the AI chip market with its H200 GPUs, enabling faster training for frontier models, while AMD launched its MI300 series. Data center expansions by Microsoft and AWS in Asia-Pacific regions accelerated compute buildout, with China's investments in sovereign AI infrastructure raising geopolitical tensions.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: How might the proliferation of open-source AI models impact global power dynamics by 2030?
